Before we start, a few short questions. Where are you leaning, and how confident are you, from 0 to 100?

I'm leaning toward keeping his return on the table, and I'd put my confidence at about 85. I also think the press coverage has run well ahead of the facts, and the board shouldn't be steered by it.
What are your top three reasons?

First, Jensen is the strategy. Our customers, partners and best engineers follow him personally, and I don't think that's easy to replace or even to measure. Second, he resigned under pressure before there were any findings, so treating that as final would be a verdict without evidence, and we owe him and the shareholders a process that finishes. Third, a permanent leadership change in the middle of an AI market sell-off could destroy far more value than this scandal ever will.

Evidence would, and only evidence. I'd also take it seriously if counsel concluded the exposure is ongoing and can't be contained. What I won't move on is anonymous sourcing and headlines, because that's exactly how a board ends up making a decision it can't undo.
